tip: 'Jangankan X, Y pun ...' = let alone X, even Y: 'jangankan naik gunung, jalan pun malas'.
'X saja yang ...' = it's only X that ...: 'minumannya saja yang berbeda' = it's only the drinks that differ.
Announcement style: 'dimohon' = 'are requested to' – in casual speech you'd just hear 'tolong'.
Station style: 'menuju' = formal 'bound for' – in conversation people just say 'ke Bandung'.
Announcement verb: 'mengalami keterlambatan' = 'is delayed' – spoken: 'pesawatnya telat'.
'Mohon perhatian' = 'attention please', the standard announcement opener; 'mohon' is a formal 'please'.
Cabin formula: 'berhenti dengan sempurna' = 'come to a complete stop' – spoken: 'benar-benar berhenti'.
Official apology: 'kami mohon maaf atas ...' = we apologize for ... – spoken: 'maaf ya, keretanya telat'.
'Dipersilakan' = formal 'are invited to' – everyday version: 'silakan ke pintu lima'.
'Harap' = formal 'please' of signs and announcements – softer than 'dilarang' (forbidden), stiffer than 'tolong'.
'Pukul sebelas' = formal clock time in announcements – in conversation people say 'jam sebelas'.
'Terlebih dahulu' = formal 'first, beforehand' – spoken Indonesian says 'duluan' or 'lebih dulu'.
'Barang bawaan' = official 'belongings, luggage' – casually people just say 'barang' or 'tas'.
'Demi' is a formal 'for the sake of': 'demi keselamatan bersama' = for our shared safety. Announcements and oaths use it; casual speech just says 'untuk'.
'Telah' = the formal 'sudah' of announcements and news – in everyday speech it's 'sudah'.
'Memakan waktu' = formal 'to take (time)' – spoken: 'perjalanannya kira-kira dua jam'.
'Mempersiapkan' = formal 'menyiapkan' (prepare) – announcements love 'memper-' verbs; spoken: 'siapkan tiketnya'.
Announcement passive: 'ditunda' = 'are postponed' – a staff member would say 'diundur'.
'Ruang tunggu' = 'waiting lounge' – official signage; in speech: 'tempat nunggu'.
'Berlaku' = formal 'applies, is valid' – you'll see it on tickets, rules and notices everywhere.
'Yang terhormat' = 'esteemed, dear' – the polite address of announcements and letters.
'Didampingi' = formal 'be accompanied' – spoken: 'anaknya harus sama orang tuanya'.
In announcements 'dapat' = 'can' – in conversation it's 'bisa': 'bisa dilihat'.
'Kami ucapkan' = ceremonial 'we express' – spoken: 'makasih ya, hati-hati di jalan'.
'Dengan hormat' = 'Dear Sir/Madam', the standard opener of official Indonesian letters.
'Bersama surat ini' = 'enclosed with this letter' – pure letter language, not something you'd say out loud.
'Atas perhatian ... terima kasih' = the fixed letter closer, 'thank you for your attention'.
'Hormat kami' = 'yours faithfully' – the letter sign-off from a team or company.
'Mengajukan permohonan' = 'to submit a request' – office language; spoken: 'minta cuti'.
'Dengan ini' = 'hereby' – a signal of formal writing; you'll almost never hear it spoken.
